newsitem.title: SYRIA: Assad tells Norway Syria still committed to peace.
newsitem.headline: Assad tells Norway Syria still committed to peace.

text.p: President Hafez al-Assad told Norway's Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal on Tuesday that Syria was still committed to making peace with Israel.
Presidential spokesman Joubran Kourieh said that Assad and Godal discussed the Arab-Israeli peace talks and "the obstacles placed by the Israeli government to block the negotiations".
"We are with peace and we want peace on the basis of the Madrid peace conference," Kourieh quoted Assad as saying.
He was referring to U.N. Security Council resolutions 242 and 338 and the land-for-peace principle on which the Arab-Israeli peace talks were based when they opened in Madrid in 1991.

Kourieh said Godal, who earlier met Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara, told Assad that he understood the difficulties facing the Middle East peace process and that he "greatly appreciated President Assad's remarks on peace".
Godal, whose country played a major role in the conclusion of a Palestinian-Israeli peace deal in 1993, came to Syria at the invitation of Shara who visited Norway in 1995.
Speaking to reporters before leaving Damascus for Jordan, Godal said his talks with Assad were "very useful".
"I discussed the situation in the Middle East in general and how to revive the stalled negotiations," he said. "We also discussed ways of boosting bilateral cooperation."

Syria has strongly condemned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for refusing to swap the occupied Arab lands for peace and for his approval for the resumption of building Jewish settlement in occupied areas.
Israel borke off peace negotiations with Syria over a year ago, before Netanyahu took office last June.
The Syrian-Israeli peace talks are stalled over the fate of the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967. Syria wants full Israeli pullback from the strategic plateau.
Godal who came from Egypt on Monday will also visit Israel and the Palestinian self-ruled areas before returning home.
